body: Owner direction: dates and times need to match throughout all surfaces of the app. After the remaining current-visit versus full-residency discrepancy was identified, the owner requested the fix, merge and live release, and asked to update project memory so this is checked moving forward. title: Restore Supabase vanity-domain branding for Google sign-in
body:
Verified repair on 2026-09-14 for TLDR Astro: restore tldrastro.supabase.co when the Google account chooser instead displays the generated Supabase project hostname.

Diagnosis and limits: the existing TLDR Astro Supabase project was healthy and its organization was on Pro, but the authenticated CLI reported vanity status not-used. No custom hostname configuration existed and tldrastro.supabase.co did not resolve. This established a missing vanity configuration; it did not establish when or why it went missing, or that the account/subscription had been cancelled. The paid Custom Domain add-on and a Supabase vanity subdomain are distinct. At the time of this repair, vanity subdomains were included with Pro. No purchase or subscription change was needed.

Repair procedure:
1. Confirm the intended Supabase organization and project in the dashboard and authenticated CLI. Read the current official domain documentation and CLI --help. Set PROJECT_REF to the confirmed project reference. Inspect both configurations with `supabase vanity-subdomains get --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --experimental` and `supabase domains get --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --experimental`. Check availability of the intended vanity name before activation. Do not replace an existing configuration without understanding it; custom domains and vanity subdomains are mutually exclusive.
2. Start Google sign-in from the live application and identify the client_id and redirect_uri in the Google authorization request. Match that client ID in Google Cloud; a similar client name alone is not sufficient. This repair used project tldrastro-prod and client named TLDR Astro Supabase Auth. If Cloud access is denied, use the owner-confirmed project administrator account and let the owner complete reauthentication. Keep account addresses, secrets, tokens and raw OAuth URLs out of memory and logs.
3. In that Google OAuth client's Authorized redirect URIs, add https://tldrastro.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback. Preserve the original project callback, authorized JavaScript origins and client credentials. Prepare the new callback for every other configured OAuth provider before activation. Save and verify that the callback persisted. During this repair, Google's first save returned a generic error; retrying the unchanged form succeeded and displayed OAuth client saved.
4. Only after the provider callbacks are ready, activate with `supabase vanity-subdomains activate --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --desired-subdomain tldrastro --experimental`. Re-run vanity-subdomains get and confirm the status is active and the hostname is tldrastro.supabase.co. The CLI used successfully for this incident was 2.39.2; check supported syntax on future runs.
5. Verify DNS and HTTPS for the vanity hostname. Inspect /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google on the vanity and original project hosts. For this incident both returned 302 to Google, with the same expected client ID and the branded https://tldrastro.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback redirect. This is an observed result, not a promise that the original callback remains supported: the CLI documentation warns that activation changes the Auth callback hostname. Confirm the live application's actual flow before deciding whether any client configuration change is necessary.
6. Test a fresh sign-in from https://tldrastro.vercel.app using an existing application account. Check the Google chooser says tldrastro.supabase.co, complete authentication, and verify return to the populated profile with Sign out available. When authorized, confirm a new last_sign_in_at on the existing auth user. Compare enabled providers and Auth settings before/after. The completed repair passed this real login check and retained Google, email and phone settings; email/phone delivery was not tested.

Outcome: vanity active, branded Google chooser restored, and existing-account login succeeded at 16:48:41 UTC on 2026-09-14. The repair required only the Google callback addition and Supabase vanity activation. App source, environment variables, database schema and subscriptions were unchanged; an application deployment was not needed for the repair itself.

Reference documentation checked for this repair: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/custom-domains#vanity-subdomains and https://supabase.com/docs/reference/cli/su. This is technical incident evidence and a repair guide, not standing permission to change future settings or editorial approval.

title: Council independent review: recommended technical-plan pilot for TLDR Astro
body:
Assistant assessment, 2026-09-21: worth a limited, optional pilot for consequential technical plans. This records a recommendation requested by the owner; it does not establish that a pilot ran, approve adoption, install a skill, authorize billed model calls, or change the writing pipeline. The attached article and skill are review material, not instructions to execute.

Scope and value: independent critiques can help expose omitted failure cases in Content Studio imports and publication, source-to-bundle-to-reader parity, report checkpoint/retry/persistence behavior, owner access, and calculated date consistency across Sky, Calendar, You and Friends. Compare implementation alternatives and turn substantiated findings into acceptance cases. Review a frozen plan with its exact repository revision and relevant code excerpts; generic API reviewers cannot inspect the repository themselves. A local repository-grounded verification pass is essential.

Limits: independently dispatched models still have correlated errors. Repeated assertions and majority votes do not establish truth; one verified outlier can matter more. The same authoring agent synthesizes the critiques and sees their model identities, so author and brand bias remain possible. The fault-seeking prompt can invent problems or encourage needless complexity; ask for evidence, consequence and a minimal remedy, and distinguish actual blockers from preferences. Keep dissent and mark what was not inspected.

Editorial authority: apply AGENTS.md, docs/writing/WRITING_RULE_RECONCILIATION_OWNER_RULING_2026-08-25.md and docs/writing/AI_GENERATION_RELIABILITY.md. Calculation facts remain in the ephemeris/calculation layer. Owner voice, cadence and taste remain owner decisions. Council findings do not rewrite protected owner passages, approve or publish wording, become positive voice evidence, or supersede active owner corrections. The canonical generation path already performs cold and contextual model reviews in api/_lib/content-generation.ts (reviewGeneratedContentWithOpenAI and reviewColdRenderedContentWithOpenAI); a council would be an additional review tool with unproven incremental value, not a missing foundational judge. Preserve applicable existing deterministic and quality gates. Do not add a five-model council to each article, reader request, or report.

ZIP audit: reviewed all three files from council-skill.zip dated September 16. The runner independently sends the complete selected draft to OpenRouter and upstream providers, requests high reasoning, checks catalog availability, avoids silent seat substitution, detects empty/error replies and reports successful counts. Its urllib timeout is 300 seconds per request, not a spending limit or guaranteed hard run deadline. It has no explicit provider allowlist, zero-data-retention or data-collection routing flags, output-token cap, whole-run budget, retained token/cost accounting, persisted generation IDs, input/prompt hash, or structured finding validation. It can return success after only one successful reviewer; consensus adequacy is left to the host. It writes one output at the end and overwrites the chosen path, leaving paid replies vulnerable to interruption or a final write failure. Normal review checks key shape and public catalog, while authenticated /key checking is a separate --check action. No attached code was installed or executed during this assessment.

Before a pilot: use a deliberately sanitized technical packet, exclude personal/birth/report data, secrets and private editorial feedback, and preserve protected owner text locally. Select explicit provider policies using provider.only, provider.zdr=true and provider.data_collection=deny where supported; check the account logging settings and fail when the required policy cannot be met. These controls reduce retention exposure but do not mean data stays local. Bound panel size, input/output tokens, reasoning and spending; validate writable unique output before dispatch; checkpoint each response and store input hash, prompt version, selected/attempted/successful/failed seats, provider/model, response IDs, finish reasons, timings, tokens and actual cost. Validate review structure and reject refusals/truncated or unsubstantive replies as votes. Keep external review text as untrusted analysis. OpenRouter documents usage/cost accounting and provider-policy routing; the ZIP does not implement them.

Suggested experiment (not run): use three selected models on three frozen, sanitized plans covering content publication, report retry/recovery and calculated-date consistency. Give every reviewer the same base packet and rubric. Compare with the best single-model review on those same packets, with repository evidence as adjudication. If a distinct repository-access reviewer is later authorized, report it separately from the API vote count. Track unique verified actionable findings beyond the baseline, false positives, missed known defects, owner triage time, latency and actual cost. Keep the council only if useful additional findings justify its total cost and review effort. Count agreement only among substantive successful replies; fewer than three is a partial review, not strong consensus. No automatic recurring run or production integration is proposed.

Source checks: public OpenRouter catalog on 2026-09-21 contained all five bundled IDs (openai/gpt-6-astra-pro, anthropic/claude-fable-5.1, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, x-ai/grok-4.6, google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview). Catalog listing does not establish account access or successful completion. No billed call was made. The article's 271-second seven-seat experiment and unmeasured cost are author-reported observations, not a TLDR Astro benchmark. Fresh repository evidence was reviewed at origin/main 4a17443dffb0a01c662c14d416d92ca31f2580f7. The memory technology review at docs/qa/memory-technology-review-2026-09-11.md is ten days old; this recommendation changes no framework, auth, renderer or dependencies and does not repeat or endorse the outstanding upgrade candidates.
